policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'After these things he departed' renders no connective; the ASV routinely leaves a resumptive δέ untranslated, so its absence does not distinguish Μετὰ ταῦτα from Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα.
ASV has the pronoun 'he departed from Athens'; had the named subject ὁ Παῦλος stood in the text the ASV would print 'Paul', as it does wherever the name is read (18:5, 18:18).
διατεταχέναι and τεταχέναι both yield ASV 'had commanded'; the compound adds nothing the English marks.
ἀπὸ and ἐκ are both rendered 'from Rome'; the preposition choice leaves no trace in the ASV.
ASV shifts subject at the verb — 'he abode with them, and they wrought' — a plural verb; the singular ἠργάζετο/εἰργάζετο would continue 'he' as the working subject.
ASV 'for by their trade they were tentmakers' renders the dative τῇ τέχνῃ and the accusative of respect τὴν τέχνην identically; the English marks no case.
ASV 'Paul was constrained by the word' renders λόγῳ; πνεύματι would give 'in the spirit'.
ASV 'testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ' supplies the copula in English either way; the presence or omission of εἶναι in the accusative construction is not visible.
ASV 'went into the house' fits εἰσῆλθεν εἰς and ἦλθεν εἰς alike; the ASV does not reserve 'entered' for the compound here.
ASV names the man 'Titus Justus', printing the praenomen Τιτίου; the omitting reading would leave only 'Justus'.
Both readings contain the same two adverbial phrases; ASV 'in the night by a vision' is a free English ordering and does not fix the Greek sequence.
ASV opens 'And he dwelt there', which renders either connective δέ or τε; the English does not distinguish them.
ASV 'when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia' renders the genitive-absolute noun-plus-participle and the single verb ἀνθυπατεύοντος identically.
ASV 'the Jews with one accord rose up' contains both elements; adverb placement in English is the translator's, so it does not settle whether ὁμοθυμαδόν preceded or followed οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι.
English requires the subject before the verb, so ASV 'This man persuadeth men' is compelled regardless of whether the Greek read ἀναπείθει οὗτος or οὗτος ἀναπείθει.
ASV renders μέν as 'If indeed' and prints no inferential particle; an untranslated οὖν is ordinary in the ASV, so its absence does not exclude the longer reading.
ASV 'if they are questions about words and names' is plural in both verb and noun, rendering ζητήματά; the singular ζήτημά would give 'if it is a question'.
ASV 'I am not minded to be a judge of these matters' prints no 'for', but the ASV leaves a weak explanatory γάρ untranslated often enough that its absence does not decide the unit.
ASV 'And they all laid hold on Sosthenes' has no subject noun; the added οἱ Ἕλληνες is a substantive the ASV would print as 'the Greeks'.

ASV 'Gallio cared for none of these things' renders μέλει; ἔμελλεν as printed by RP is an itacistic spelling of the same imperfect in this idiom, not the verb 'was about to', so the English does not exclude it.
ASV 'having shorn his head in Cenchreae' places object before adverbial phrase as English requires; the Greek order of τὴν κεφαλήν and ἐν Κεγχρεαῖς is not recoverable from it.
ASV 'And they came to Ephesus, and he left them there' has a plural verb of arrival distinguished from the following singular, which is κατήντησαν; the singular Κατήντησεν would give 'he came'.
διελέξατο and the deponent aorist διελέχθη both yield ASV 'reasoned with the Jews'.
ASV 'when they asked him to abide a longer time' has no prepositional phrase; the added παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς would appear as 'with them'.

ASV subordinates the leave-taking as a participle — 'but taking his leave of them, and saying ... he set sail' — with the single finite verb at the end, which is ἀποταξάμενος καί; the RP finite ἀπετάξατο would give 'but he took his leave of them'.
ASV reports only 'I will return again unto you if God will'; the added clause about keeping the coming feast at Jerusalem has no counterpart in the verse.
ASV 'I will return again unto you' prints no connective inside the quotation, but an untranslated δέ is ordinary in the ASV and does not exclude the longer reading.
ASV 'establishing all the disciples' renders στηρίζων and ἐπιστηρίζων alike; the prefix is not marked in the English.
ASV 'taught accurately the things concerning Jesus' names Jesus, and does so in a verse that has already used 'the Lord' for the way; κυρίου would give 'the Lord' again.
ASV 'when Priscilla and Aquila heard him' keeps Priscilla first; the ASV does not reorder coordinated proper names, so the English follows Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας.
ASV 'the way of God' is the only English order available for either Greek arrangement of ὁδόν and τοῦ θεοῦ.
